newsitem.title: MOZAMBIQUE: Mozambique, Zimbabwe sign iron ore accord.
newsitem.headline: Mozambique, Zimbabwe sign iron ore accord.

text.p: The Mozambican and Zimbabwean governments on Friday signed a declaration of intent to produce hot briquetted iron (HBI) using Zimbabwean iron ore and Mozambican natural gas.

The gas will come from the Temane gasfield in the southern Mozambican province of Inhambane, and will require a 450 km long pipeline to carry it to the planned iron ore reduction plant which will be built on the Mozambique-Zimbabwe border.

A separate agreement to carry out a feasibility study on the project was signed by representatives of South African mining company JCI Ltd, the Mozambican National Hydrocarbon Company (ENH), Zazara Petroleum of the United Arab Emirates, and the Atlantic Richfield Company (ARCO) of the United States.
Zazara is the original option-holder on the Temane gas field, and it has brought in ARCO to help develop the field.

The project envisages that JCI, together with Zimbabwean company BIMCO, will mine and beneficiate iron ore in the Zimbabwean midlands and then rail it to the border where it will be reduced into "hot briquetted iron". This will then be exported to buyers in the Middle East and Pacific Rim via the port of Beira.
HBI is a particularly pure form of iron, and can be mixed with scrap metal to produce high quality steel in electric arc furnaces.
The feasibility study should be complete by October 1997, and if it goes ahead investors believe they could be in production by the end of the year 2000.
The reduction plant will produce about 2.8 million tonnes of iron ore to two million tonnes of HBI per year and will use about 100 million cubic feet of gas per day.
